overview: This bill would bar people convicted of fraud involving certain pandemic-era relief programs from getting further financial help from the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that backs loans and grants for small businesses. It covers convictions for financial misconduct or false statements tied to Paycheck Protection Program loans, COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans, Restaurant Revitalization Fund grants, and Shuttered Venue Operators Grants. The ban applies to owners of more than 20 percent, officers, directors, and key employees, and to any business that has such a person involved. It applies only after all appeals are finished, and it still allows SBA disaster loans. It would not affect government contracts signed before the bill becomes law. As of April 1, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say taxpayers shouldn't keep funding people who were convicted of stealing from pandemic relief programs, and the bill protects SBA programs for honest small businesses.
against: Critics say barring entire businesses because of one associate's conviction could hurt employees and co-owners who did nothing wrong, and that existing penalties and debarment rules may already address the problem.
